**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 85, verse 4 (part 1 of 2):**

﴿Killed were the People of the Trench﴾, meaning: cursed. "Al-ukhdud" (the trench) is a long cut in the earth, like a river. Its plural is "akhadid." Scholars differed concerning them:

Abu Hamid Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Salihi informed us; Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Sa'dan al-Khatib informed us; Abu Ahmad Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Quraysh ibn Nuh ibn Rustam informed me; Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Bushanji narrated to us; Hudbah ibn Khalid narrated to us; Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us; Thabit al-Bunani narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Suhayb, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There was a king among those who came before you, and he had a sorcerer. When the sorcerer grew old, he said to the king: 'I have grown old, so send me a boy whom I may teach sorcery.' So he sent him a boy. On his way to the sorcerer, the boy would pass by a monk, sit with him, and hear his words, and they pleased him. So whenever he came to the sorcerer, he would pass by the monk and sit with him. When he came to the sorcerer, the sorcerer would beat him; and when he returned from the sorcerer, he would sit with the monk and hear his words, and when he came to his family, they would beat him. So he complained [[Addition from manuscript B.]] of that to the monk. The monk said: 'When you come to the sorcerer, say: "My family detained me." And when you come to your family, say: "The sorcerer detained me."' While he was in that state, he came upon a huge beast that had blocked the people's way. He said: 'Today I will know whether the monk is better or the sorcerer.' So he took a stone and said: 'O Allah, if the affair of the monk is more beloved to You than the affair of the sorcerer, then kill this beast so that the people may pass.' He threw it and killed it, and the people passed. He came to the monk and informed him. The monk said to him: 'My son, you are today better than me. Your affair has reached what I see, and you will be tested. If you are tested, then be patient and do not reveal me.' The boy would heal the blind and the leper and treat people for all other ailments. A companion of the king, who had gone blind, heard of him and brought him many gifts, and said: 'All of this is yours if you cure me.' He said: 'I do not cure anyone; it is Allah who cures. If you believe in Allah, I will pray to Allah for you, and He will cure you.' So he believed in Allah, and Allah cured him. He went to the king and sat with him as he used to. The king said to him: 'Who restored your sight?' He said: 'My Lord, the Mighty and Majestic.' He said: 'Do you have a lord other than me?' He said: 'My Lord and your Lord is Allah.' So the king seized him and continued to torture him until he pointed to the boy. The boy was brought, and the king said to him: 'My son, your sorcery has reached the point that you heal the blind and the leper, and you do such and such.' He said: 'I do not cure anyone; it is Allah who cures.' So the king seized him and continued to torture him until he pointed to the monk. The monk was brought, and it was said to him: 'Return from your religion.' He refused, so the king called for a saw, placed it at the middle of his head, and split him with it until both halves fell. Then the king's companion was brought and it was said to him: 'Return from your religion.' He refused, so the saw was placed at the middle of his head and he was split until both halves fell. Then the boy was brought and it was said to him: 'Return from your religion.' He refused, so the king handed him over to a group of his companions and said: 'Take him to such and such a mountain, climb with him, and when you reach its summit, if he returns from his religion [well and good], otherwise throw him down.' They took him and climbed the mountain with him. He said: 'O Allah, suffice me against them however You will.' The mountain shook beneath them and they fell. He came walking back to the king, who said to him: 'What became of your companions?' He said: 'Allah sufficed me against them.' The king then handed him over to another group of his companions and said: 'Take him and carry him in a boat to the deep part of such and such a sea. If he returns from his religion [well and good], otherwise throw him into the sea.' They took him, and he said: 'O Allah, suffice me against them however You will.' The boat capsized with them and they drowned. He came walking back to the king, who said to him: 'What became of your companions?' He said: 'Allah sufficed me against them.' Then he said to the king: 'You will not kill me until you do what I command you.' He said: 'And what is that?' He said: 'Gather the people on one open plain, crucify me on a trunk, then take an arrow from my quiver, place the arrow in the belly of the bow, and say: "In the name of the Lord of the boy," then shoot me, for when you do that, you will have killed me.' So he gathered the people on one open plain, crucified him on a trunk, then took an arrow from his quiver, placed the arrow [[Omitted in manuscript A.]] in the belly of his bow, then said: 'In the name of [Allah] [[Addition from manuscript B.]] the Lord of the boy,' then shot him. The arrow struck his temple, so he placed his hand on his temple at the spot of the arrow, and died. The people said: 'We believe in the Lord of the boy,' three times. The king was informed and it was said to him: 'Have you seen what you were fearing? By Allah, your fear has come upon you. The people have believed.' So he ordered the trench to be dug at the mouths of the lanes; it was dug, fires were kindled in it, and he said: 'Whoever does not return from his religion, throw him into it,' or it was said to him: 'Jump in.' They did so, until a woman came with a small child of hers, and she hesitated to fall into it. The boy said to her: 'O mother, be patient, for you are upon the truth.'"

This is a sound hadith, related by Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj from [Hudbah ibn Khalid, from] [[Omitted in manuscript B.]] Hammad ibn Salamah. [[Narrated by Muslim in the Book of Zuhd, chapter on the story of the People of the Trench, the sorcerer, the monk and the boy, no. 3005 (4/2299).]] Hammad ibn Salamah.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from Wahb ibn Munabbih that a man had remained upon the religion of Jesus, and came to the people of Najran [and called them] [[Omitted in manuscript B.]], and they responded to him. Dhu Nuwas, the Jew, marched against them with his troops from Himyar and offered them the choice between the fire and Judaism. They refused him, so he dug the trenches and burned twelve thousand people. Then, [when] [[Omitted in manuscript B.]] Aryat overcame Yemen, Dhu Nuwas fled, plunged into the sea with his horse, and drowned. [[Sirat Ibn Hisham: 1/32–37. See also: al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya of Ibn Kathir: 2/119–121; al-Kafi al-Shaf p. 183.]] Al-Kalbi said: Dhu Nuwas killed Abd Allah ibn al-Tamir.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq also said, from Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr: A ditch was dug in the time of Umar ibn al-Khattab, and they found Abd Allah ibn al-Tamir with his hand placed on a wound in his head; when his hand was lifted from it, blood gushed forth, and when it was left, it returned to its place. On his hand was an iron ring inscribed: "My Lord is Allah." When this reached Umar, he wrote: "Return him to the state in which you found him." [[See: Sirat Ibn Hisham: 1/37–38.]]

Ata narrated from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: In Najran there was a king of the kings of Himyar called Yusuf Dhu Nuwas ibn Shurahbil ibn Sharahil, in the interval [before the Prophet's birth by seventy years]. [[Omitted in manuscript B.]] In his land there was a boy called Abd Allah ibn Tamir, whose father had entrusted him to a teacher to teach him sorcery. The boy disliked this but found no alternative to obeying his father, so he kept going to the teacher. On his way there was a monk of beautiful recitation and a lovely voice, and this pleased him. He mentioned something close in meaning to the hadith of Suhayb, until the boy said to the king: "You cannot kill me unless you do what I tell you." He said: "How shall I kill you?" He said: "Gather the people of your kingdom while you are on your throne, and shoot me with an arrow in the name of my God." The king [did that] [[Omitted in manuscript B.]] and killed him. The people said: "There is no god but Allah; Abd Allah ibn Tamir, there is no religion but his religion!" The king grew angry, closed the gate of the city, seized the mouths of the lanes, dug a trench, filled it with fire, and then presented them to him one by one. Whoever returned from Islam he left alone, but whoever said, "My religion is the religion of Abd Allah ibn Tamir," he threw into the trench and burned. In his kingdom there was a woman who had embraced Islam along with those who had embraced it, and she had three children, one of whom was a suckling infant. The king said to her: "Return from your religion, or I will throw you and your children into the fire." She refused, so he seized her eldest son and threw him into the fire. Then he said to her: "Return from your religion," but she refused, so he threw the second into the fire. Then he said: "Return," but she refused. They then took the infant from her to throw him into the fire. The woman was about to return, but the infant said: "O mother, do not return from Islam, for you are upon the truth, and there is no harm upon you." The infant was thrown into the fire, and his mother was thrown after him. [[See: al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya of Ibn Kathir: 2/121.]]

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Ibn Abza said: When the people of Isfandhar were defeated, Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "What rulings apply to the Magians, since they are not People of the Book?" Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Yes, they did have a Book. Wine had been permitted to them, and a king of theirs drank it until it overcame his reason, and he took his sister and had intercourse with her. When the intoxication left him, he regretted it and said to her: 'Woe to you! What is this that I have done, and what is the way out of it?' She said: 'The way out is that you address the people and say: "Allah has permitted marriage to sisters." Then, when it has spread among the people and they have forgotten it, you address them and forbid it.' So he stood up to preach and said: 'Allah has permitted you to marry sisters.' All the people said: 'God forbid that we should believe in this or acknowledge it! No prophet has brought it to us, and no Book has been revealed to us concerning it.' So he lashed them with the whip, but they refused to acknowledge it, so he drew the sword against them. They refused to acknowledge it, [so he dug a trench for them] [[Omitted in manuscript A.]], kindled fires in it, and presented them to it. Whoever refused and did not obey him, he cast into the fire, and whoever agreed, he let go his way." [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 30/132.]]

Al-Dahhak said: The People of the Trench were from the Children of Israel. They seized men and women, dug a trench for them, kindled fires in it, and made the believers stand over it, saying: "Will you disbelieve, or shall we cast you into the fire?" It is claimed that they were Daniel and his companions. This is the narration of al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both. [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 30/133. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/65 to Ibn al-Mundhir.]]

Abu al-Tufayl said, on the authority of Ali, may Allah be pleased with him: The People of the Trench had a prophet who was Abyssinian; a prophet [was] [[Omitted in manuscript B.]] sent from Abyssinia to his people. Then Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, recited: ﴿And We did send messengers before you; of them are those We have related to you﴾ [Ghafir: 78]. He called them, and some people followed him, so he fought them. His companions were killed and captured, and he was bound, and not one of them escaped. Then they dug a trench and filled it with fire. Whoever followed the Prophet was thrown into it, and whoever agreed with them was left alone. They brought a woman with a suckling infant, and she was distressed, so the infant said: "O mother, go forward and do not be hypocritical."

[[Omitted from "a".]] As for the one in al-Sham, it was Abtamus the Roman; as for the one in Persia, it was Bukhtnassar (Nebuchadnezzar); and as for the one in the land of the Arabs, it was Dhu Nuwas Yusuf.
